newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European shares open mixed, dollar firms.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European shares open mixed, dollar firms.

text.p: Concerns over U.S. interest rates persisted in Europe's equity markets on Thursday and shares were mixed in early trade, while the dollar firmed a touch.
British stocks climbed slightly but hopes of a short-term push to the psychologiaclly important 4,000 level were receding once more.
Modest profit-taking on Wall Street, which fell 11.47 points to 5877.36 on Wednesday, set the tone for trading in the London and elsewhere.

The U.S. interest rate concerns ahead of the Federal Reserve Open Market Committee meeting on September 24, which many feel will increase rates, coupled with caution ahead of Friday's expiry of FTSE 100 futures and options, are set to cap activity.
"We're Wall Street-waiting and Wall Street-watching," said one London trader. "But, while there is momentum for the market to go up it could still find it difficult to breach 4,000."
After opening lower, the FTSE 100 reversed the early fall and was showing a modest rise of 9.8 points to 3,965.5 soon after 0900 GMT.
Squaring of books by market-makers ahead of Friday's expiry were behind the turnaround, said dealers.

"The word is out with the market-makers that they want to square up their positions in case there are violent movements tomorrow," said one senior trader."I don't think there's anything outside that, full stop."
Bid speculation resurfaced early on with further buying interest on the back of talk that Germany's Bayer might be a predator for British pharmaceutical group Zeneca.
"Zeneca keeps blowing hot and cold but one day we'll come in and there'll be a bid for the company," said the trader.
Zeneca shares added 24p to 1,567-1/2p.
French stocks opened weaker, retraced their fall to trade slightly higher, but then fell again and the CAC index was down 1.98 at 2070.75 at 0900 GMT.
Pinault-Printemps-Redoute was the top gainer on the CAC, rising more than three percent after reporting a jump in first-half profit on Wednesday.

German shares opened mostly flat but then edged lower after data showing German August money supply growth came in above forecasts and a new business climate index showed confidence improving slightly.

In the foreign exchanges, the dollar rose slightly against the mark and the yen in early European business after clawing its way up from lows overnight. But in the low volume conditions dealers were looking at another quiet day's range trading.

The dollar sank more than a yen after disappointing U.S. trade data on Wednesday which also hit its value against the mark. "After its tumble yesterday the dollar will struggle to regain its footing, with rallies increasingly being seen as opportunities to sell into," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered.

Strong psychological support at 110 yen has now turned into resistance and will prove a hard nut to crack given the current propensity to take quick profits, dealers said. The jump in the U.S. trade deficit to $11.68 billion in July from $8.19 billion in June took a market expecting a figure nearer $9.0 billion by surprise. Analysts said it has again got the market thinking about the September 24 FOMC and what will happen to interest rates.
They said the rise in the deficit suggests weak growth in the third quarter and puts a question mark over the need for a rate rise in the near term. CURRENCIES AT 0900 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5100 marks and 109.45 yen compared with 1.5091 marks and 109.12 yen in Europe late on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0900 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares rose 9.8 points to 3,965.5.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index fell 1.98 points to 2,070.75.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt fell 3.96 to 2,621.74.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened steady at $383.40 after closing in London at $383.35 on Wednesday.
